'''Chandler Hutchison''' (born April 26, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player who most recently played for the [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State Broncos]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.broncosports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/chandler_hutchison_914762.html|title=Chandler Hutchison}}</ref>

==High school career==
Hutchison lettered three years at [[Mission Viejo High School]]. As a junior, he averaged 13.8 points and 4.8 rebounds while leading Mission Viejo to the regional quarterfinals of the [[California Interscholastic Federation|CIF]] Southern Section 1AA Tournament.

In his senior season, he was ranked No. 80 in the ESPN Top 100 and the No. 7 prospect in California<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/172531/chandler-hutchison|title=Chandler Hutchison - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-04-08}}</ref> and a consensus 4 star recruit by 247 Sports. He averaged 19.5 points and led Mission Viejo to the CIF Southern Section title game and regional quarterfinals of CIF State Championship tournament.

==College career==
Hutchison posted 3.1 points per game as a freshman and started in the NCAA Tournament matchup versus [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]].<ref name="walton">{{cite news|last1=Walton|first1=Brandon|title=Boise State set to say farewell to Chandler Hutchison on Senior Night|url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/basketball/boise-state-set-to-say-farewell-to-chandler-hutchison-on/article_117f361a-5914-591c-b45f-25b2dd2c9e2a.html|accessdate=April 8, 2018|work=Idaho Press|date=March 2, 2018}}</ref> He averaged 6.8 points and 4.1 rebounds per game as a sophomore in 2015–16. With the departure of [[James Webb III]], coach [[Leon Rice]] began to look at Hutchison as more of an offensive threat, and he responded by hitting the weight room and remaking his jump shot. He had a breakout season as a junior, averaging 17.4 points, 6.8 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game wile shooting 37.7% of his threes.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Fischer|first1=Jake|title=Chandler Hutchison is the NBA Draft’s Hidden Gem|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2017/12/13/nba-draft-chandler-hutchison-boise-state-weber-state-damian-lillard|accessdate=April 8, 2018|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=December 13, 2017}}</ref> He declared for the [[2017 NBA Draft]] but returned to the Broncos. Hutchison had a stellar senior year, averaging 20 points and 7.7 rebounds per contest.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Roberts|first1=Rachel|title=From ‘soft, immature, entitled’ to the ‘best player in Boise State history’|url=http://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-basketball/article199924644.html|accessdate=April 8, 2018|work=[[Idaho Statesman]]|date=February 13, 2018}}</ref> As a senior, he was named to the First-team All-[[Mountain West Conference]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Zeigler|first1=Mark|title=SDSU's Malik Pope named second team all-conference|url=http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/sd-sp-sdsu-basketball-malik-pope-second-team-20180306-story.html|accessdate=April 6, 2018|work=[[San Diego Union-Tribune]]|date=March 6, 2018}}</ref> Hutchison was a Top-10 Finalist for the [[Jerry West Award]] and a Top-30 Finalist for the [[Naismith Trophy]].<ref name="walton"/>
